note: Data/model quality monitoring, drift detection, and evaluation.

children.note: AI Gateway-enabled payload logging to Unity Catalog Delta tables; captures request/response for debugging, model quality analysis, and compliance audits. Legacy format deprecated Apr 30, 2026.
Automated calculation of quality metrics (null counts, distinct values, min/max, quantiles, standard deviation, frequent values) with baseline and consecutive-window comparisons.
Single-point-in-time profiling of table state; captures baseline metrics for comparison with future windows; creates reference profile for anomaly detection.
Consecutive sliding-window profiling over time; tracks metric evolution across commits; enables trend detection and comparative window analysis.
Profile tracking for model inference requests captured in inference tables; monitors prediction payload distribution and output characteristics over time.

Numeric drift tests (Kolmogorov–Smirnov, Wasserstein distance, PSI) and categorical drift tests (chi-square, total variation, Jensen–Shannon) on predictions and features; baseline or consecutive-window comparisons.

Three statistical tests for continuous distributions: Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS) test for shape differences, Wasserstein distance for distribution shift magnitude, Population Stability Index (PSI) for category distribution stability.

Three statistical tests for discrete distributions: chi-square test for independence, total variation distance (TV) for probability mass differences, Jensen–Shannon (JS) divergence for symmetric KL divergence.
Automatic monitoring of table freshness (learns commit patterns, flags late updates) and completeness (predicts row-volume bounds, flags drops) using historical patterns.
Define aggregate metrics (raw table columns), derived metrics (computed from aggregates), and drift metrics (time-window or baseline comparisons); minimize recomputation by layering.
Direct computations from raw table columns (count, min, max, mean, stddev, distinct, null_count); reusable base layer for derived metrics.
Computed from aggregate metrics using custom SQL expressions; enables domain-specific KPIs and composite quality indicators.
Comparison of current window metrics against baseline or previous window; detects statistical shifts in aggregate and derived metrics.
Auto-generated profile-metrics tables; Lakeview visualization; configurable Databricks SQL alerts on quality/drift metrics with email, webhook, Slack, or PagerDuty notifications.
Interactive visualizations of profile metrics and drift results; pre-built dashboard templates for quality monitoring; supports custom parameterization.
Databricks SQL alert rules triggered on metric thresholds or anomaly detection; configurable refresh intervals and escalation logic.
Multi-channel alert delivery: email, webhook (HTTP POST), Slack (channels, direct messages), PagerDuty integration for on-call escalation.
8 built-in LLM judges (Correctness, RelevanceToQuery, RetrievalRelevance, etc.) for GenAI; custom LLM and code-based scorers; deterministic + heuristic evaluation; reusable across dev and production.
Run evaluation scorers on sampled production traffic; collect human feedback via Review Apps; combine with LLM judges for continuous quality, safety, and latency tracking with dashboards.

note: Automation, bundles, and pipelines from dev to prod.

children.note: Official reference templates combining ML code, bundle configuration, and CI/CD workflows for GitHub Actions / Azure DevOps; implements dev → staging → prod workflow with PR-triggered tests.
Infrastructure-as-code in YAML for ML projects; defines jobs, pipelines, experiments, models, endpoints, permissions; centralized configuration management for reproducible deployments.
Define Lakeflow Jobs in bundle YAML; specify triggers, tasks, runtime config, and dependencies for orchestrated ML workflows.
Define Lakeflow Pipelines (DLT) in bundle config; declarative ETL pipelines with SQL/Python code and quality expectations.
Define model registry entries and aliases in bundles; bind models to experiment runs, enable versioning, and manage stage promotion workflows.
Define MLflow experiment configuration in bundle YAML; organize tracking experiments across workspaces.
Define model serving endpoints in bundle config; manage scaling, traffic splitting, and feature serving integration.
Define fine-grained access control for all resources in bundle; grant roles (viewer, editor, owner) to users and groups at object level.
DAG-based orchestration with task dependencies, serverless execution, up to 1000 tasks per job; supports repair runs and complex control flow across multiple tasks.
Cron schedules, Delta table updates, file arrivals, model-registry events (Beta), continuous loops, and API-triggered runs; multi-trigger per job (Beta) with up to five triggers.
Time-based job execution via cron expressions; supports UTC or workspace timezone configuration.
Job runs initiated on Delta table commit detection; combines with file triggers for data-arrival workflows.
Triggers on cloud object storage path events (S3, ADLS, GCS); supports wildcard patterns for flexible file detection.
Triggers on model-related events: transition to production, new version registered, or tag changes; enables automated deployment pipelines (Beta).
Job that continuously runs in a loop with configured interval; minimal latency between completions.
Manual job execution via REST API or UI; supports dynamic parameter passing at run time.
Declarative ETL with SQL/Python support, auto-scaling, and built-in data quality expectations; three violation policies (Warn/Drop/Fail) with different row-handling behavior.
Native DLT SQL syntax for table and view definitions; automatic dependency inference and incremental computation.
@table and @view decorators for Python functions; enables complex imperative logic within declarative pipeline framework.
Row-handling policies on quality constraint violations: Warn (log only), Drop (skip row), Fail (halt pipeline); supports delta.quality expectations metadata.
Native Git version control (now called Git Folders); multi-branch support, merge conflict resolution, notebook versioning, and CI/CD automation via Repos API.

children.n: CI/CD with GitHub Actions & Azure DevOps
children.note: Workflow templates for bundle validation, testing, deployment across dev/staging/prod; integrates with MLOps Stacks for automated release management.
Infrastructure-as-code for workspace, catalogs, clusters, permissions; manages resources at account and workspace levels; separate from bundle layer; production-grade support.

note: Python, R, Spark, Ray and deep-learning frameworks.

children.note: Core ML libraries preinstalled on ML runtimes: pandas (data manipulation), scikit-learn (algorithms), XGBoost/LightGBM (boosting), statsmodels (statistics).
Data manipulation and analysis library; Runtime 19 ML includes 2.3.3; cornerstone of single-node analytics and feature engineering.
Classification, regression, clustering, feature engineering; Runtime 19 ML includes 1.7.2; top-tier support for traditional ML workflows.
Gradient boosting library; Runtime 19 ML includes 3.2.0; production-grade boosting for tabular data at scale.
Fast gradient boosting; Runtime 19 ML includes 4.6.0; community-integrated alternative to XGBoost with memory efficiency.
Statistical modeling and hypothesis testing; available on ML runtimes; complementary to scikit-learn for classical statistics.
Multi-language runtime support via %r magic command in notebooks; requires dedicated compute (not standard/serverless). SparkR deprecated in Runtime 16.0+; migrate to sparklyr.
Distributed data processing framework; core Databricks compute engine for parallel DataFrame operations on massive datasets; supported on serverless, standard, and dedicated compute.
Distributed ML library built on Apache Spark; classification, regression, clustering, collaborative filtering; pyspark.ml API for scalable ML pipelines on distributed data.
Framework-agnostic distributed computing for hyperparameter tuning (Ray Tune), distributed training (Ray Train), and data processing; integrates PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face.
PyTorch (top-tier GA support 2026; 2.12.0 on Runtime 19 ML) and TensorFlow (legacy; removed from Runtime 18.0+; available on Runtime 17.3 LTS with 2.19.0).
Top-tier GPU-native deep learning framework; CPU and GPU builds preinstalled on ML runtimes; Runtime 19 ML includes 2.12.0.
Legacy framework; removed from Runtime 19 ML; available on Runtime 17.3 LTS (2.19.0); open-source TensorFlow incompatible with latest CUDA; slated for removal.
Spark DataFrames with pandas-compatible API; seamless scaling from single-node pandas to distributed pyspark.pandas for data engineering workflows.
NLP library by John Snow Labs; tokenization, NER, embeddings, text processing on Spark; community-integrated for production-grade NLP at scale; available via Partner Connect.
